result: NK cell activity was markedly decreased in almost all CFS patients vs healthy controls, with normal NK (CD16+/CD56+), T and B cell counts.
reason: Independent 1994 cohort measuring NK functional activity, same direction as the older reduced-cytotoxicity literature; not among cited studies.

result: CFS CD8+ T cells showed reduced CD11b and raised CD38 and HLA-DR (with raised CD28 in many), suggesting expanded activated cytotoxic T cells; T-cell proliferation was normal.
reason: Surface activation markers by flow cytometry are not the transcriptional/chromatin exhaustion signature the finding claims; activation is arguably the opposite phenotype, and no atlas finding covers CD8 activation markers.

result: Enterovirus RNA by PCR was found in muscle of 32/121 (26.4%) CFS vs 20/101 (19.8%) other neuromuscular disease controls, not significant, failing to confirm the group's earlier 53% vs 15% result.
reason: Tests persistent EV RNA by PCR in a larger cohort and finds no difference; muscle not stomach, but the finding's detail explicitly covers the inconsistent muscle EV evidence this paper belongs to.

result: Blinded, sensitivity-optimised PCR and Southern blot found no HTLV-I/II, human spuma, simian, bovine, feline or gibbon ape retroviral sequences in blood of 21 CDC-surveillance CFS patients or 21 matched controls.
reason: Paper did not test XMRV/pMLV, so it cannot bear on the contamination finding; it is an older targeted-PCR null for viruses in blood, closest to the blood virome null finding.

result: In 12 male CFS vs 13 male controls, 30 min of 40% MVC isometric handgrip produced no change in plasma IFN-gamma, IFN-alpha, IL-1beta or TNF-alpha up to 24 h, and patients' POMS fatigue, depression and confusion decreased.
reason: Measures post-exertion blood cytokines, not PEM onset/duration; a small, admittedly insensitive null for exercise-induced blood immune changes.

result: Blinded neuroradiologist reads found abnormal brain MRI in 27% of 52 CDC-criteria CFS vs 2% of 52 matched controls (white-matter T2 hyperintensities in 9 vs 1, ventricular/sulcal enlargement in 5), though 3 patients with hyperintensities had other probable medical causes.
reason: Same measure (routine clinical MRI reads) with a positive difference, against the finding's claim of no consistent abnormality; controls were headache/trauma referrals.

result: In 12 CFS vs 12 sedentary controls, quadriceps MVC, 20:50 Hz force ratio and relaxation rate were normal at rest and up to 48 h after incremental cycling, exercise duration was similar, and perceived exertion relative to heart rate was higher (by 3.2 Borg units).
reason: No sustained-task fatigability or brain motor-network measure; perceived exertion is a different variable. The muscle-recovery data are covered by the grip-fatigability link.

result: Quadriceps maximal voluntary and stimulated force and recovery for 48 h after a symptom-limited cycle test were normal in 12 CFS vs 12 sedentary controls, with higher perceived exertion in patients.
reason: Measures voluntary strength and post-exercise strength recovery (as in Paul 1999 in the finding) and finds no difference, so it contradicts rather than extends.

result: Light and electron microscopy of 108 CFS/muscle-pain patients vs 22 volunteers showed no consistent relation of symptoms to fibre type, size, degeneration/regeneration, glycogen or mitochondrial abnormalities, and quadriceps contractile function was normal before and 48 h after exercise.
reason: Independent older biopsy series finding normal/nonspecific histology, as the finding claims; not among cited studies.

result: During sustained maximal tibialis anterior contraction, CFS patients had significantly lower voluntary activation than controls, while fatigue, muscle metabolism, M-wave and twitch tension were normal.
reason: Supports a central contribution by a different method (central activation failure), but fatigability itself was normal, so not a replication of earlier fatigue with reduced brain activation.
